meta.name: Post PR preview page screenshots to GitHub pull requests with Snapshot Site

name: Screenshot PR Preview Pages → GitHub PR Comment

parameters.content:
## Screenshot PR Preview Pages → GitHub PR Comment

### How it works

Your CI job calls this workflow's webhook once a pull-request preview deployment is live, POSTing `owner`, `repository`, `prNumber`, the preview base URL and — the important part — a `pages` array holding **only the routes the pull request actually touched** (built from `git diff --name-only`). A Code node joins each `path` onto `previewUrl` (handling a trailing slash on the base and a leading slash on the path without producing `//`), rejects any URL that is missing its `https://` scheme, drops duplicate routes and caps the run at `maxPages` (10 by default). A single 30-second Wait lets the preview deployment warm up, then the loop takes one page per iteration through a Snapshot Site **Screenshot** call — WebP, 1280px wide, full page, cookie banners hidden — and records one row per page (label, URL, returned image `link`, `ok` / `failed`). Hard failures (network/HTTP after 3 retries) and soft failures (HTTP 200 + `{error: true}`) both land on the same recorder marked `failed`, and the loop keeps going. When the loop finishes, one Code node renders every row into a single GitHub-flavoured markdown body — a summary table, one collapsible embedded screenshot per captured page, and a clearly separated "could not be captured" block — and the GitHub node posts it as **one comment** on the pull request.

### Setup steps

- Install the `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site` community node (Settings → Community nodes → Install → `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site`) — verified by n8n.
- Add a Snapshot Site credential and a GitHub credential (classic PAT with `repo`, or a fine-grained token with **Pull requests: Read and write** on the target repo).
- `owner`, `repository` and `issueNumber` on the GitHub node are all driven by the webhook payload, so one workflow serves every repo that calls it — nothing to hardcode.
- Activate the workflow and copy the Webhook node's **Production URL** (the Test URL only listens while the editor is open).
- Call it from your preview-deploy job with `{"owner":"your-org","repository":"your-repo","prNumber":123,"previewUrl":"https://pr-123.preview.example.com","commit":"a1b2c3d","maxPages":10,"pages":[{"path":"/","label":"Home"},{"path":"/pricing","label":"Pricing"}]}`.
- Build `pages` from the PR's diff, not from a static list — the README has a copy-pasteable GitHub Actions step that maps `git diff --name-only` to routes. Skip the call entirely when the diff touched no pages.
- `previewUrl` must be a full URL including `https://` — the API rejects bare domains with a soft error (HTTP 200 + `{error: true, message}`), so **Build Preview Page List** rejects the payload up front, before the wait and before any capture is billed.

### Customization

`format: "webp"` keeps a 6-image PR comment light; switch **Capture Preview Page** to `format: "png"` (one field) if your GitHub instance proxies WebP badly. Raise or lower `maxPages` in the payload to change the per-run cap, and `width` (390 for a mobile review pass) to change the viewport. Add `hide: ".announcement-bar, #chat-widget"` to `additionalFields` so chat widgets and A/B banners stay out of the screenshots. To review *changes* rather than *pages*, swap the Screenshot call for a **Compare** against the same route on production — see workflow 20.

## Receive the PR and pick only the changed pages

CI posts the routes the pull request touched, so the workflow never screenshots the whole site.
**Build Preview Page List** joins each path onto the preview base URL, validates the `https://` scheme, dedupes repeated routes and caps the run — all before the wait, so a bad payload costs zero API calls.
The 30s Wait fires **once** for the whole run, not per page: preview deployments are often cold, and a capture taken during a cold start is a screenshot of a spinner.

## Capture each page and handle errors

One Screenshot call per changed page: WebP, 1280px, full page, cookie banners hidden.
Hard failures (error output, after 3 retries) and soft failures (`{error: true}` on the success output) are both recorded as a `failed` row and returned to the loop. One unreachable preview URL is a line in the comment, never a lost comment.

## Post ONE comment on the pull request

On the loop's Done branch every row is rendered into a single markdown body — table, embedded screenshots, failure block.
One comment per run on purpose: 10 captured pages must not mean 10 notifications for every reviewer subscribed to the PR.
